title: Tiered trial taper + credit top-ups to improve PLG conversion for heavy developer accounts
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Run a controlled experiment to evaluate a two-part intervention for new free-tier and trial users: (A) a 'tapered trial' that reduces credit expiry pressure by offering predictable, timed top-ups for accounts that reach specific usage thresholds, and (B) contextual upgrade touchpoints that surface tailored messaging and price-snippets when usage patterns indicate conversion intent. Motivation: previous experiments (see related PM tickets) show conversion drop-offs when credits expire abruptly. Hypothesis: smoothing perceived time-to-value (via top-ups) + timely upgrade prompts will increase trial->paid conversion by 20% for mid/high-usage cohorts while keeping net revenue per converted user neutral or positive.
experiment_design: Cohorts: new signups over a 6-week window split into three cohorts: control (baseline 14-day credits), Variant A (tapered top-ups), Variant B (tapered top-ups + contextual upgrade prompts).
Tapered top-ups: initial grant = 3,000 tokens; when an account consumes >=70% before day 7, grant an automatic top-up of 1,500 tokens and extend expiry by 7 days (max one top-up).

Contextual upgrade prompts: triggered when account meets 2 conditions: (1) >=70% credit consumption OR >2500 tokens/day for 2 consecutive days, AND (2) uses a monitored endpoint type (chat/generation/embeddings). Messaging variants include 'Boost now', 'Reserved capacity trial', and 'Commit to save' (A/B within Variant B).
Randomization: hashed by account id to ensure even distribution across company domains and geos. Stratify by expected monthly spend bucket (low/med/high) estimated from signup form answers.
Duration: 6 weeks active + 4 weeks observation for conversion to paid and revenue impact.
acceptance_criteria: Implementation of credit top-up automation in billing service with audit logs and metrics emitted to the console (events: topup_granted, topup_claimed, topup_expired).
Frontend hooks for contextual prompts with experiment flags and 3 messaging variations. Design sign-off on copy and CTA.
Instrumentation: cohort assignment, impressions, clicks, upgrade flows, conversion, MRR attribution. Dashboards live in Growth BigQuery + Looker tile.
Safety guard: we must be able to quickly revoke top-ups and disable prompts if fraud or abuse spikes; runbook documented in Confluence.
metrics: Primary: trial->paid conversion rate within 30 days by cohort (target +20% relative lift for Variant B over control).
Secondary: ARPU of converted users, freemium churn rate, net-new revenue delta, support ticket volume (fraud/credit disputes).
Operational: number of top-ups issued, % of top-ups consumed, errors in top-up pipeline, latency of prompt render (<250ms).
Safety: abnormal account activity rate post-topup (flag if >3x baseline).
rollout_plan: Week 0: finalize spec, engineering tickets, and design assets. Week 1: ENG implements top-up service + feature flag; DES provides prompt variants and UTM tracking. Week 2: internal dogfood with Redwood dev accounts and 48h smoke tests. Week 3-8: experiment active across signups, monitoring daily; mid-point review at Week 5. Week 9-12: analyze results, stakeholder review, and decision (kill/iterate/rollout).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Top-ups could be gamed by creating many accounts. Mitigation: throttle top-ups per payment instrument and add heuristics (device fingerprint, IP rate limit).
Risk: Increased support volume due to confusion about expiry extensions. Mitigation: clear email/SMS notifications and in-product banner explaining top-up rules.
Risk: Revenue cannibalization if cheap top-ups replace paid upgrades. Mitigation: cap total top-ups per 90 days and analyze ARPU delta by cohort.
notes: Design feedback (03/13): use 'Extend & Explore' copy language instead of 'Free top-up' — less likely to train users to expect endless free credits (DES-228 review).
Engineering note (03/14): will reuse existing billing webhook and emit new event names; ENG-4144 required for quota enforcement and audit trails.
PM decision log: prioritize high-usage developer cohort first; if positive signal, follow with enterprise-friendly variant that teases Dedicated pricing.
